title: Business Value and Configuration Decisions
readerIntent: Decide which differences belong in configuration and which require implementation.
summary: Configuration shortens customer delivery when a difference changes policy or operating choices but preserves the capability contract.

sections.heading: Business outcomes
items: Reuse one framework across customers and environments without maintaining forks.
Separate developer-owned defaults from operator-managed deployment and secret values.
Review material runtime changes before activation and retain an audit history.
Roll back governed configuration without rebuilding unrelated application code.
Keep behavior differences visible to people and AI development tools.

sections.heading: Decision rule
paragraphs: Use configuration when the capability and authority remain the same but a value, selection, threshold, mapping, provider, or enabled behavior varies. Extend an existing service or contract when the algorithm or business rule changes. Add a new capability only after confirming that no existing extension point owns the requirement.

sections.heading: Who benefits
items: Business owners gain reusable products that can serve different customers without maintaining framework forks.
Business users gain approved tenant or operational choices without waiting for a code release where runtime governance applies.
Developers gain discoverable defaults and extension boundaries instead of scattered constants.
Operators gain environment-specific control, validation, audit, and rollback.
Security reviewers gain explicit ownership for secrets, permissions, exposure, and sensitive changes.

sections.heading: Configuration examples
items: Select a cache, database, search, messaging, or AI provider through the owning provider-neutral capability.
Choose active modules and remote module endpoints for a server topology.
Set bounded timeouts, retry policies, page sizes, cache lifetimes, token budgets, and operational thresholds.
Enable versioning or publishing only for modules whose data requires that lifecycle.
Configure employee idle-lock behavior or other BackOffice runtime policy through a persistent governed setting.

sections.heading: What is not configuration
items: A new business algorithm requiring different code and tests.
Executable source embedded in stored configuration.
A credential committed to properties.js.
A package.json object containing normal application behavior.
A frontend flag intended to bypass backend authorization or validation.
A second loader or registry that competes with Nodics runtime authority.

sections.heading: Cost and risk trade-offs
paragraphs: More configurable behavior can reduce customer-development effort, but every option increases validation, documentation, test, support, and upgrade responsibility. Expose a property only when variability is a real product requirement and a safe default exists.
Runtime configurability adds operational speed but also raises change risk. Sensitive values may need preview, approval, staged activation, observation, and rollback rather than immediate mutation.

sections.heading: Decision example
paragraphs: If one retailer wants a 60-second stock cache lifetime and another wants 30 seconds, the cache contract can expose a bounded property. If a retailer wants a fundamentally different stock-allocation algorithm, that belongs in an inventory service extension, not a configuration expression.

If the difference applies only to local testing, place it at the local environment layer. If it is a governed tenant policy, use the supported tenant or runtime contract. Do not duplicate the property in several scopes without defined precedence.

sections.heading: Governance questions
items: Who owns the default and who may override it?
Is the value public configuration, sensitive secret material, or executable behavior?
At which application, environment, server, node, tenant, or customer scope should it differ?
Can it change safely at runtime, or does it require a restart?
What validation, approval, audit, monitoring, and rollback evidence is required?

sections.heading: Evidence for an adoption decision
items: The effective value can be explained from defaults and selected layers.
Invalid values fail safely before dependent behavior becomes ready.
One tenant, server, or environment cannot leak its override into another.
Secrets are absent from source, generated packs, logs, errors, and browser responses.
Runtime activation and rollback retain actor, scope, version, and result evidence.
The original reusable behavior remains unchanged when the override is absent.
